calls.head: Stars collide: Miller vs. Konecny
calls.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Miller’s line (Kartye, Miller and Perreault) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Flyers’ first line is Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kartye’s late goal lifts the Rangers past the Flyers
paras: Gabe Perreault got the scoring started for the Rangers early in the first, but Simon Benoit scored his first goal for Philadelphia midway through the second to tie it 1-1. Noel Acciari put the Flyers up 2-1 just under two minutes later, and that was all they would get. Pavel Dorofeyev tied it up for the Rangers on the power play with just over six minutes left. Tye Kartye put the Rangers ahead for good with less than five minutes left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Dylan Garand made 23 saves for the Rangers, and Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. The Rangers improved to 9-7-1, third in the Metropolitan, while the Flyers fell to 4-10-4, still last in the Metropolitan.
